messages.subject: 3 dimensional IRT Model estimation.
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run the following model
*******************************
votes_code<- '
data {
  int<lower=1> J;              // number of legislators
  int<lower=1> K;              // number of votes
  int<lower=1> N;              // number of observations
  int<lower=1> G;              // number of groups
  int<lower=1,upper=J> jj[N];  // legislator for observation n
  int<lower=1,upper=K> kk[N];  // vote for observation n
  matrix[N,G] x; // group indicators
  vector[N] y;                 // position for observation n
}


parameters {    
  matrix[J,G] alpha;               //  
  matrix[K,G] beta;                // 
  real mu_beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma_beta;
  matrix<lower=0>[K,G] gamma;
  real mu_gamma;
  real<lower=0> sigma_gamma;}


transformed parameters 
{{matrix[N,G] summands;
for (g in 1:G)
for (n in 1:N)
summands[n,g]<- (x[n,g]*gamma[kk[n],g])*(alpha[jj[n],g] - beta[kk[n],g]);
}{
vector[N] total;
for (n in 1:N)
for (g in 1:G)
total[n] <- sum(summands[n,g]);
}}



model {
for (g in 1:G)
alpha[g]~ normal(0,1);         

for (g in 1:G)
beta[g] ~ normal(mu_beta, sigma_beta);
mu_beta~ normal(0, 1);
sigma_beta ~ cauchy(0,1);

for (g in 1:G)
gamma[g] ~ lognormal(mu_gamma, sigma_gamma);
mu_gamma ~ normal(0, 1);
sigma_gamma ~ cauchy(0,1);

y ~ bernoulli_logit(total); }'


votes_dat<-list(N=66281, J=445, K=159, G=2, jj=politician_id_numeric, kk=action_id_numeric, y=vote_1, x=matrix(group, nrow=66281))

******************************************************

I am getting following error:

TRANSLATING MODEL 'votes_code' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'votes_code' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE - DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

variable "summands" does not exist.
variable "summands" does not exist.


LOCATION OF PARSING ERROR (line = 33, position = 16):

PARSED:

transformed parameters 
{{matrix[N,G] summands;

for (n in 1:N)
summands[n,g]<- (x[n,g]*gamma[kk[n],g])*(alpha[jj[n],g] - beta[kk[n],g]);
}{
vector[N] total;
for (n in 1:N)
for (g in 1:G)
total[n] <- sum

EXPECTED: "(" BUT FOUND: 

(summands);
}

*************************************
The error is arising from the summation term. Here, my goal is to get a code that will run the following expressions through n observations

y[1] ~ bernoulli_logit( (x[1,1]*gamma[1,1](alpha[1,1] - beta[1,1]) + (x[1,2]*gamma[1,2](alpha[1,2] - beta[1,2]) + ..........+ (x[1,g]*gamma[1,g](alpha[1,g] - beta[1,g]))

Thank you in advance,

Yusuf

parts: There’s a reason people go crazy for indenting. Rewrite your transformed parameters block as

transformed parameters
{
{
matrix[N,G] summands;
for (g in 1:G)
for (n in 1:N)
summands[n,g]<- (x[n,g]*gamma[kk[n],g])*(alpha[jj[n],g] - beta[kk[n],g]);
}
{
vector[N] total;
for (n in 1:N)
for (g in 1:G)
total[n] <- sum(summands[n,g]);
}
}

Not sure what you were trying to do, but the braces inside transformed parameters are defining
local scopes, any all variables created inside of them disappear as soon as the scope ends. In
particular, any variables you want saved need to be outside of any scope.

You could include both summands and total as transformed parameters

transformed parameters
{
matrix[N,G] summands;
vector[N] total;

for (g in 1:G)
for (n in 1:N)
summands[n,g]<- (x[n,g]*gamma[kk[n],g])*(alpha[jj[n],g] - beta[kk[n],g]);

for (n in 1:N)
for (g in 1:G)
total[n] <- sum(summands[n,g]);
}

or if you just want total,

transformed parameters
{
vector[N] total;

{

matrix[N,G] summands;
for (g in 1:G)
for (n in 1:N)
summands[n,g]<- (x[n,g]*gamma[kk[n],g])*(alpha[jj[n],g] - beta[kk[n],g]);

for (n in 1:N)
for (g in 1:G)
total[n] <- sum(summands[n,g]);
}
}

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] 3 dimensional IRT Model estimation.
parts:
Hi Yusuf,

There's an issue with scoping within your transformed parameters block. I've reformatted that section just so it's clearer. (If you haven't seen the Stan emacs mode, I'd suggest trying it out.)

transformed parameters {
  {
    matrix[N,G] summands;
    for (g in 1:G)
      for (n in 1:N)
        summands[n,g]<- (x[n,g]*gamma[kk[n],g])*(alpha[jj[n],g] - beta[kk[n],g]);
  }
  {
    vector[N] total;
    for (n in 1:N)
      for (g in 1:G)
      total[n] <- sum(summands[n,g]);
  }
}

The summands variable is only valid within the first set of nested braces. It is treated as a local variable and both summands and total will not be available in the other blocks.

Hopefully that clears things up. Once again, I'd highly suggest using the Stan emacs mode, or any editor that handles C++-like formating to help with indentation and scoping.



Daniel
